## 2018 Toyota Corolla in Vancouver: Buy-Check Snapshot
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/car-front.svg

A 2018 Corolla with **86,000 miles (~138,000 km)** can still be a solid commuter car if the inspection is clean. With a **CAD 1,200 first-year repair budget**, the key question is whether the brake squeal is just pads/rotors or a sign of bigger wear, and whether the car’s maintenance history is complete.

## Pre-Purchase Inspection and Cost Guide
| Area | What to Check | Why It Matters | Typical Cost in Vancouver (CAD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brakes | Pad thickness, rotor wear, caliper sticking, brake fluid age, road test squeal | Occasional squeal may be normal, but worn pads/rotors can eat most of your budget | 180–550 |
| Tires | Brand/date code, tread depth, even wear, alignment signs | “New tires” only helps if they’re quality and correctly installed/aligned | 0–180 |
| Battery/Charging | Battery age, alternator output, parasitic drain | Recent battery replacement is good, but confirm the charging system is healthy | 0–180 |
| Engine bay | Oil leaks, coolant level/color, belts, hoses, air filter | Prevents surprise cooling or lubrication repairs | 0–250 |
| Transmission | Smooth shifts, no shudder, fluid condition, no delayed engagement | CVT issues are expensive if neglected | 0–250 for service check; much more if faulty |
| Suspension/Steering | Clunks, struts, bushings, tie rods, wheel bearings | Common wear item on higher-mileage commuter cars | 0–300 |
| Undercarriage/Rust | Brake lines, exhaust, pinch welds, floor rust, accident repairs | Vancouver moisture and winter road use can accelerate corrosion | 0–300 |
| Electronics | ABS light, check-engine light, windows, AC, infotainment | Small issues can still add up | 0–200 |
| Service Records | Oil changes, brake service, coolant, transmission service, recalls | A complete history lowers risk more than cosmetic condition | 0 |

## First-Year Maintenance Costs to Watch
- **Brake pads only:** CAD 180–300
- **Pads + rotors:** CAD 350–550
- **Brake fluid flush:** CAD 120–180
- **Oil change service:** CAD 80–140
- **Cabin + engine air filters:** CAD 50–120
- **Wheel alignment:** CAD 120–180
- **Transmission service check/service:** CAD 180–300
- **Battery/charging follow-up:** CAD 0–180
- **Suspension wear fix allowance:** CAD 150–400

Likely first-year total if the car is healthy: **CAD 400–900**
If brakes and one wear item need attention: **CAD 900–1,400**

## Buy or Pass Decision Framework
### Reasonable buy if:
- Brake squeal is only **light pad wear** and rotors are still serviceable
- The car has **clean service records**
- No warning lights, no accident damage, no rust concerns
- A mechanic confirms **no suspension, transmission, or cooling issues**
- The seller price still leaves room for **CAD 600–1,200** in first-year maintenance

### Be cautious if:
- Brake squeal comes with **pulsation, grinding, or pulling**
- Tires are “new” but cheap, mismatched, or badly aligned
- Battery was replaced because of repeated no-start problems
- Maintenance history is incomplete
- The inspection finds any **CVT, rust, or suspension** problem

### Best decision rule for your budget:
- If the inspection shows only **brakes + fluid/service items**, this is likely a **reasonable buy**
- If it needs **brakes plus suspension or transmission work**, it likely **exceeds your first-year budget**
- If the seller won’t allow a pre-purchase inspection, treat that as a **strong warning sign**
